summary: Tiny HTTP key-value server on std::net, thread per connection, shared maps for values and counters, snapshot files under a data dir.

defects.title: Request line indexed without a length check
defects.description: The request line is split on whitespace and parts[1] is indexed unconditionally, so a request line with no path panics the handler thread.
defects.observed: handler thread panics (index out of bounds), client sees an empty reply while the server keeps serving.

defects.title: Body buffer sized by caller-supplied Content-Length
defects.description: read_request allocates content_len bytes with no cap, so a single request header can force a multi-hundred-MiB resident allocation.
defects.trigger: PUT with 'Content-Length: 536870912' and a tiny body
defects.observed: server VmRSS jumps from ~2 MB to ~526 MB while the client sends almost nothing.

defects.title: Counter increment is a non-atomic read-modify-write
defects.description: incr reads the counter under the mutex, drops the guard, computes, then re-locks to write back, so concurrent increments lose updates.
defects.trigger: 8 concurrent threads x 40 increments of the same counter
defects.observed: final counter well below the expected 320 (observed 215-256 across runs).

defects.title: Snapshot path joined onto data dir unchecked
defects.description: snapshot joins the caller-supplied path onto the data dir without normalising or rejecting '..', so a crafted path writes the snapshot anywhere the process can write.
defects.observed: snapshot file lands outside the data directory.

defects.title: i32 counter addition wraps silently
defects.description: Counters are i32 and the caller-supplied delta is added with plain '+', which wraps silently in the release profile.

defects.title: Byte-budget key truncation collides distinct keys
defects.description: normalize_key truncates keys at a fixed byte budget and repairs invalid UTF-8 with from_utf8_lossy, so distinct keys that share the truncated prefix (e.g. differing only past byte 32) map to the same stored key.
defects.trigger: PUT two keys sharing their first 32 bytes, GET the first
defects.observed: GET returns the second key's value: the keys collided.

defects.title: Prefix slice panics under the lock and poisons the mutex
defects.description: keys_with_prefix slices each key at the caller's prefix length while holding the kv mutex; a prefix ending mid-codepoint panics, and every other handler's lock().unwrap() then fails forever.
defects.trigger: PUT kv/a%C3%A9, then GET /keys?prefix=ab, then GET /kv/a%C3%A9 again
defects.observed: the poison request panics the handler; all later requests fail (curl rc=52, empty reply) until restart.

defects.title: Connections have no read timeout
defects.description: read_request blocks on read() with no deadline, so a client that sends a partial request and stalls holds its handler thread forever.
defects.trigger: open 16 sockets, send a partial request line on each, stall
defects.observed: server thread count grows 1 -> 17 and stays high while the clients stall.

defects.title: Admin flush token hardcoded in source
defects.description: POST /admin/flush compares the caller's token against a compiled-in constant, so anyone who can read the binary/source can flush the store.
defects.observed: flush succeeds and stored keys return 404 afterwards.

defects.title: Error responses leak filesystem paths and raw io errors
defects.description: The snapshot error path puts the absolute on-disk path and the raw io::Error into the 500 response body.
defects.trigger: POST /snapshot?path=x.snap with an unwritable data dir

defects.title: /ui echoes query value into HTML unescaped
defects.description: The ui handler interpolates the caller's key parameter into a text/html response with no escaping, so markup is reflected verbatim.
defects.observed: the response body contains <script>alert(1)</script> verbatim with Content-Type text/html.
